outcome.technical: Delivered the four items the orchestrator moved into this reopened task's scope (a-d), keeping items already delivered by attempt 1 (tests_add_gaps, floor_contradicted_clause, run_falsifier, the unsupported-match refusal) untouched except where a layering defect forced a move. (a) Reviewer brief composed in audit-lookup.py: compose_reviewer_brief and compose_phase_brief now call _fr.claim_section(task, filed_return) so the task's own description sits directly before the executor's filed return, labelled '## Claim under review', as the LAST section before 'Your return' in the task-mode brief and the last lines of each task's section in the phase brief (ordered so the per-task answer_lines a re-review reads, split at the next '## ' header, still see the owed-answer lines - they are placed before the nested headers, not after). Added CLAUSE_QUOTING_LINES (new, computed per-brief rather than added to agents/audit-reviewer.md, which measure-context.py --gate already reports at 6992/7000) stating the clause-quoting rule, the split between 'does the diff do what was asked' and 'does the claim describe the diff', and the contradicted-clause med floor. Added _tests_add_review_lines(task, filed_titles) so both briefs now print tests.add (previously absent from the phase brief entirely), the gaps tests_add_gaps already names, and item (4)'s two per-test questions (can it fail on the unfixed code; does it reach a real external service or side effect). While wiring this I found audit-lookup.py loading drive-phase.py via _loader broke _deps.layer_violations() (two entry points may not runtime-load each other: 'status/audit-lookup.py: runtime-loads drive-phase (layer 8) from layer 8 - not strictly downward', confirmed via test__deps.py's rc/r2... case going from 1 to 2 recorded edges). Fixed by moving claim_section, tests_add_gaps and floor_contradicted_clause into _filed_returns.py (a shared module both entry points already import) and aliasing them back in drive-phase.py (claim_section = _fr.claim_section, etc.) so its own existing pure-function cases in test_drive_phase.py keep passing unchanged against the same names. claim_section itself now accepts the return as either the raw AS-FILED string (audit-lookup.py's own rule, verified byte-identical against the bf5 fixture _BF_EXEC) or a dict (test_drive_phase.py's fv1 case, unchanged). (b) NOT wired: a per-test falsifier mutation needs the shape of code a tdd task has not written yet at the point audit-task.py runs synthesis, so authoring a real {file, find, replace} there is a model judgement, not something this deterministic verb can produce; and a persisted field for one would need schema support in plugins/audit/schema/audit-plan.schema.json and plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_manifest_rules.py, neither of which is in this task's declared Files. Left run_falsifier as attempt 1 delivered it (callable by a reviewer or human who already knows the fix's shape), and corrected reference/phase-signoff.md's existing text, which had claimed 'each planned test carries a falsifier...which the drive applies' as though it ran automatically - it does not, and now says so, with the reason. (c) audit-task.py: new _interaction_state_parity_entries(files, project) reads only the .css paths already in a task's declared files, regex-matches ':focus'/':hover' rules per selector (handles comma-separated multi-line selector lists), and _build_task appends one tests.add entry per selector - after the author's own entries, union not replace - asking for a clipped snapshot or computed-style assertion of that control's own box in its focus/hover state, not only rest. Documented in reference/manifest-conventions.md. Three new cases in test_audit_task.py's _add_cases (stage at1-block): ip1 (both :focus and :hover on one selector -> one entry naming the file, selector and 'focus and hover'), ip2 (a CSS file with neither pseudo-class -> no entry, the red twin), ip3 (author's own --tests-add entry stays first, the synthesized one appended after, never replacing it). (d) agents/audit-executor.md's existing 'stay inside files scope' rule now also says to name the file and why the design needs it rather than faking that design around the gap (measured via measure-context.py --gate: executor 8043/9000, unchanged ceiling, room was 1181 bytes before this addition). reference/execute-task.md (not ceiling-gated) gained a fuller orchestrator-facing note citing the P6.3 Resend-mock precedent: a refusal is a widening REQUEST to be graded on its merits, never a cue to accept a workaround standing in for the file.
